report:
## Cranberry Products and Prevention of Recurrent Cystitis in Women: Evidence Summary

**Conclusion: Yes, cranberry products can help reduce recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs/cystitis) in women, though the effect is modest and depends heavily on formulation and dose.**

**The strongest evidence** comes from the updated **Cochrane systematic review** (2023, 50 trials, 8,857 participants), which found cranberry products reduced symptomatic, culture-verified UTI risk by roughly 26%, with benefits concentrated in women with a history of recurrent UTIs, children, and other high-risk groups (https://gizmodo.com/cranberry-juice-prevent-urinary-tract-infection-science-1850363312; https://specialistnutritionrehab.co.uk/does-cranberry-juice-and-or-d-mannose-prevent-recurrent-utis/).

**However, earlier individual trials were mixed.** A well-known 2011 double-blind RCT of cranberry juice (319 college women) found no significant reduction in recurrent UTI (https://academic.oup.com/cid/article-abstract/52/1/23/406427). This inconsistency likely reflects differences in proanthocyanidin (PAC) concentration—juice often lacks sufficient active dose, while concentrated extracts perform better.

**Dose matters.** Standardized high-dose PAC extract trials (≥36 mg PAC/day) show clearer benefit than low-dose formulations. A 2021 RCT comparing high- vs. low-dose PAC extract in 145 women with recurrent UTI, and a 2024 meta-analysis of RCTs specifically evaluating cranberry prophylaxis in women, both support efficacy at adequately dosed extracts (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12894-021-00811-w; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2024.1422121/full).

**Comparative effectiveness:** A JAMA Internal Medicine noninferiority trial found cranberry capsules were less effective than low-dose antibiotics for recurrence prevention, though still confer some benefit as a lower-risk alternative to reduce antibiotic resistance concerns (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/fullarticle/1105854).

**Bottom line:** Cranberry extracts—particularly standardized, higher-PAC formulations—show a moderate but real preventive effect against recurrent cystitis in women, per the highest-quality Cochrane evidence, though plain juice's efficacy is less certain.
